answer: Each applicant earns one amateur radio callsign with a proctored 50-question exam, a 35 dollar fee, and a 120 dollar radio registered by serial number. Over 60 days the operator logs 30 contacts, each confirmed by the other station and stamped with a cipher. One contact must reach a repeater on a mesa, and one must cross the lagoon. A forged log fails when the other station denies it, cancelling it for a year. Forging 1,000 callsigns needs 1,000 exams and 30,000 fake contacts, like 1,000 fake pilot licenses no plane will fly, so every fake burns cash and airtime before earning a cent.
